title: Telemetry decision lab notes + rollforward playbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact working notebook for making bounded telemetry decisions ahead of model and infra rollouts. Goal is to record tradeoffs (cost / signal fidelity / operator ergonomics), surface owned dashboards, and provide a short rollforward playbook when signals degrade post-release. This is intentionally pragmatic: pick small, measurable changes we can reverse.

Context and motivation:
- Rollout cadence has shortened: more feature/model pushes per week. We need a lightweight process for changing telemetry during a rollout (sampling, probe cadence, new metrics) without exploding query costs or operator toil.
- Past incidents show we often add lots of traces/metrics reactively and then forget to prune; this doc tries to lock down decision criteria and ownership.

Quick glossary (how I use terms here):
- Probe: a synthetic or instrumented check (meter, counter, trace anchor) used in rollouts.
- Probe-group: set of probes that map to one operator dashboard.
- Rollforward: the action taken after a failed rollback window (i.e., continue deployment with mitigations).
- Signal budget: a weekly query/trace budget allocated to a feature rollout.

Decision heuristics (short):
1) Signal first for user-facing regressions. Any instrumentation that helps detect visible latency/hallucination/user-error gets priority.
2) Cost cap per rollout: default 15% extra telemetry spend for a 2-week canary; opt-in for higher budgets from product/infra.
3) Trace sampling: prefer severity-weighted adaptive sampling vs naive uniform sampling. Default policy: 1% uniform + 100% for error paths and 10% for tail-latency buckets.
4) New metric name hygiene: must include component, probe-group, and rollout id as labels (e.g. inference.kv_warmth.canary-202601).
5) Dashboard ownership: whoever authors the rollout telemetry is the temporary owner for 2 weeks; ownership must be handed to an owner in the operator roster or Product once stable.

Trace design notes:
- Span naming: use short stable verbs (eg: req.tokenize -> req.model.encode -> req.kv.hit). Avoid embedding rollout ids in span names; use attributes/tags instead.
- Low-overhead anchors: create a single trace anchor at entry and attach lightweight child spans only on errors or >p95 latencies. Avoid always-on deep tracing for high-throughput endpoints.
- Session provenance: add a session_id/hash at root span so traces can be stitched across microcalls without leaking PII. PII fields must be hashed per privacy guidelines.
- Trace-retention tiers: keep full traces for error-worse-than-SLO for 14d, sampled traces at 0.5% for 30d, and summary rollups indefinitely.

Metric definitions (working table, one-per-line):
- inference.request.count: counter; increments on API acceptance; label: model, route, rollout_id. Use for throughput and burst detection.
- inference.latency.ms: histogram; bucketed (0-50,50-200,200-500,500-2000,2000+); labels: model, route, cache_hit. Primary SLI input.
- kv.cache.hit_ratio: gauge; compute per tenant and global; label: model_family, rollout_id. Helps explain latency regressions.
- gen.token.hallucination_rate: ratio; numerator = moderated_hallucination_count, denominator = reviewed_responses. Only computed in evaluation cohorts.
- rollout.telemetry.cost_delta: gauge; weekly delta in query/trace cost attributable to rollout. Owners must keep <= budget.

Dashboard ownership & minimal widget checklist (create these or verify existing):
- Rollout summary card: throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, kv_hit_ratio, telemetry cost delta. Owner: rollout author.
- Operator-investigation card: recent traces sample link (errors+tails), top error messages, top tenant contributors to errors. Owner: observability oncall.
- Cost-control card: query counts, trace counts, cost by probe-group. Owner: infra-costing.
- Release gate widget: boolean pass/fail for smoke probes and canary SLIs. Owner: product-release lead.

Rollforward playbook (step-by-step, rapid):
1) Detect: if canary SLI breaches for >2 consecutive 5m windows OR unexplained operator tickets > threshold, open a rollforward decision ticket.
2) Triage quick-hypotheses: (a) telemetry noise, (b) KV cold starts, (c) model quality regression, (d) infra degradation. Use the Rollout summary card and top-tail traces to pick 1–2 hypotheses.
3) Mitigate: increase probe sampling on the suspected domain by 5–10x (capped) and tag traces with 'triage=true'. If cost budget would be exceeded, temporarily redirect sampling to a focused tenant cohort.
4) Short-term mitigations to deploy with rollforward: enable fallback model variant, disable non-critical batching, increase KV prefetch for warm cohorts. Each mitigation must have an owner and revert-command.
5) Observe 30–60 minutes. If >80% confidence hypothesis resolved the issue, mark rollforward success and schedule cleanup (prune probes added) in 48h. Otherwise, escalate to oncall lead and consider rollback.

Cleanup and telemetry debt rules:
- Any probes added temporarily for triage must have a TTL tag and an auto-prune ticket created within 24h.
- Long-lived probes (more than 2 weeks) require a short rationale: owner, retention tier, expected query cost, and rollback condition.
- Metric name deprecation: add a deprecated alias metric for 1 week before deleting any named metric; keep the alias mapping in the decision ticket.

Experimentation notes and open questions:
- Should we support a per-release telemetry budget tradeoff flow in the console? (Leah investigating UX)
- Can we automate severity-weighted adaptive sampling in the tracing backend? Prototype exists in github:repo/telemetry-probes#42 but needs infra cost modeling.
- How to make trimmed synthetic probes that approximate user journeys while avoiding session-level PII? Proposal: hashed session id + synthetic user cohort.

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Aisha: draft a minimal console wireframe for telemetry budget opt-in (due 2026-01-22).
- Marco: spike adaptive sampling prototype integration with trace backend; estimate cost impact (due 2026-01-18).
- Leah: add a release-gate widget stub to the rollout dashboard and assign temporary owner mapping (due 2026-01-12).
- Nikhil: create automation that enforces TTL tags on probes added by rollout PRs; short ticket created (JIRA:OBS-4872).

Notes to self / loose ideas (scratch):
- Consider a "telemetry-mode" label on routes: minimal | standard | verbose. Allow feature flagging to flip modes for specific tenants.
- Small-o experiment: sample 1% of tenant ids uniformly but 20% of top-10 tenants to preserve signal for heavy users while bounding costs.
- Keep a weekly telemetry budget dashboard for infra/product to see cumulative spend by active rollouts.

Unresolved questions to discuss in next sync:
- exact p95 sampling multiplier when enabling triage traces (1x->10x?),
- retention tiers for sampled traces for evaluation cohorts,
- who approves >15% telemetry budget increases for enterprise customers.

End of notes. This is a working doc — expect edits and small forks per-rollout. If you copy/clone it into a confluence page, add the rollout id and link back to the originating PR in the linked_artifacts list.
